scope.summary: BodyKit end-to-end lifecycle test per Section 13.27 — the full loop, no-context provable: NL description -> author_body -> channel edits -> configure_genitals -> corrective re-bake -> garment drape via the Cloth bridge -> export through ue_fbx_bridge and blender_gltf -> every descriptor green -> EventLedger replay reconstructs identical state, driven exclusively through MCP tools.
acceptance_criteria: One test drives the complete chain through MCP tools ONLY (no internal API shortcuts): author_body from an NL description -> edit_body channel adjustments toward an archetype-(a)-class build -> configure_genitals (arousal + state sweep on a futa variant leg) -> corrective re-bake job -> starter-garment drape via the Cloth bridge -> export_body on ue_fbx_bridge and blender_gltf.

All applicable descriptors report green at their stages: BODY_TOPOLOGY_VALID, BODY_DECOUPLE_VALID, BODY_POSE_RANGE_VALID (QA pose smoke), GENITAL_BLEND_VALID, EXPORT_BODY_VALID, LICENSE_GUARD untripped.
EventLedger replay from genesis reconstructs the identical final BodySpec, avatar row, recipe, and export manifest hashes (TAI-OVR-007 parity proven for the whole BodyKit lifecycle).
The flow is executable by a no-context model: every step's inputs derive from prior tool outputs plus the UserManual chapter — asserted by the test using only documented wire contracts.
The test runs in the CI long lane within budget; each stage emits its Flight Recorder events (verified event sequence).
scope.risk_if_missed: All 176 BodyKit MTs pass individually while the assembled lifecycle breaks at a seam nobody owns — the exact integration failure mode packet-level tests exist to catch, on the module the operator's production pipeline will stand on.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Backend/solver scope: behavior is observable via TraceProjection, typed TAILOR_BODY_* receipts, and the 13.12 capture APIs; operator/model GUI exposure rides the BodyKit panes (13.27) and is validated there.

target_entries: Tailor UserManual > BodyKit jobs, diagnostics, and recovery

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.reason: This MT owns authoritative, job, or external-tool lifecycle events and must project the same event_id, run_id, actor_id, and correlation_id from EventLedger into Flight Recorder.
This MT must wire the shared internal_diagnostics API for its native, job, device, solver-run, or DCC failure modes with bounded structured evidence.
Long-running, native, or external-process work must register bounded progress and child/process identity with the shared Palmistry watcher; Tailor must not fork a watcher.

risks: Broad MT scope can hide multiple review targets.
Markdown MT lists may disagree with packet-declared active/next MT truth.
Receipt routing may target an old MT if contract identity is omitted.
minimum_controls: Exactly one primary proof target per MT unless the packet records why not.
MT identity must be stable and referenced by receipt correlation.
Generated projection drift must not wake Coder or Validator by itself.

required_changes_before_execution: Do not close the original lifecycle until native UX, PoseKit/character interlink, BodyKit creator tooling/assets, anatomy, DCC, visual, and performance hardening pass.
Consume the signed technical refinement, canonical command/surface registries, classified HBR tiers, and task-oriented UserManual contract before execution.
